adhkar_ayat_al_kursi.title: Ayat al-Kursi
adhkar_ayat_al_kursi.arabic: أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيمِ. اللَّهُ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ ۚ لَا تَأْخُذُهُ سِنَةٌ وَلَا نَوْمٌ ۚ لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ ۗ مَنْ ذَا الَّذِي يَشْفَعُ عِنْدَهُ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِ ۚ يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ ۖ وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِشَيْءٍ مِنْ عِلْمِهِ إِلَّا بِمَا شَاءَ ۚ وَسِعَ كُرْسِيُّهُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ ۖ وَلَا يَئُودُهُ حِفْظُهُمَا ۚ وَهُوَ الْعَلِيُّ الْعَظِيمُ
adhkar_ayat_al_kursi.meaningEn: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah—there is none worthy of worship except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of all. Neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. None can intercede except by His permission. He knows what is before and behind them, and they encompass nothing of His knowledge except what He wills. His Kursi extends over the heavens and the earth, and preserving them does not tire Him. He is the Most High, the Most Great.
adhkar_ayat_al_kursi.transliteration: Aʿūdhu billāhi min ash-shayṭānir-rajīm. Allāhu lā ilāha illā huwa al-Ḥayyul-Qayyūm, lā ta'khudhuhu sinatun wa lā nawm, lahu mā fis-samāwāti wa mā fil-arḍ, man dhal-ladhī yashfaʿu ʿindahu illā bi'idhnih, yaʿlamu mā bayna aydīhim wa mā khalfahum, wa lā yuḥīṭūna bishay'in min ʿilmihi illā bimā shā', wasiʿa kursiyyuhus-samāwāti wal-arḍ, wa lā ya'ūduhu ḥifẓuhumā, wa huwal-ʿAliyyul-ʿAẓīm.
adhkar_ayat_al_kursi.purposeEn: Reported protection from jinn from the morning until the evening.
adhkar_ayat_al_kursi.eveningPurposeEn: Reported protection from jinn from the evening until the morning.
sources: Hisn al-Muslim 75; Qur’an 2:255; Al-Hakim 1/562; Sahih at-Targhib wa at-Tarhib 1/273
Hisn al-Muslim cites Al-Albani grading the protection report authentic. The source does not prescribe three repetitions; this entry is one recitation in the morning and one in the evening.

adhkar_al_ikhlas_3.title: Surah Al-Ikhlas
adhkar_al_ikhlas_3.arabic: قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ, اللَّهُ الصَّمَدُ, لَمْ يَلِدْ وَلَمْ يُولَدْ, وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌ
adhkar_al_ikhlas_3.meaningEn: Say: He is Allah, the One; Allah, the Self-Sufficient. He neither begets nor is born, and there is none comparable to Him.
adhkar_al_ikhlas_3.transliteration: Qul huwallāhu aḥad. Allāhuṣ-ṣamad. Lam yalid wa lam yūlad. Wa lam yakun lahu kufuwan aḥad.
adhkar_al_ikhlas_3.purposeEn: Together with Al-Falaq and An-Nas, reciting this three times in the morning is reported to suffice as protection against everything.
adhkar_al_ikhlas_3.eveningPurposeEn: Together with Al-Falaq and An-Nas, reciting this three times in the evening is reported to suffice as protection against everything.
sources: Hisn al-Muslim 76; Qur’an 112:1-4; Abu Dawud 4/322; at-Tirmidhi 5/567
Hisn al-Muslim gives Al-Ikhlas, Al-Falaq and An-Nas as three recitations each in the morning and evening and cites Al-Albani’s Sahih at-Tirmidhi.

adhkar_al_falaq_3.title: Surah Al-Falaq
adhkar_al_falaq_3.arabic: قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ الْفَلَقِ, مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ, وَمِنْ شَرِّ غَاسِقٍ إِذَا وَقَبَ, وَمِنْ شَرِّ النَّفَّاثَاتِ فِي الْعُقَدِ, وَمِنْ شَرِّ حَاسِدٍ إِذَا حَسَدَ
adhkar_al_falaq_3.meaningEn: Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of daybreak from the evil of what He created, from the evil of darkness when it settles, from the evil of those who blow on knots, and from the evil of an envier when he envies.
adhkar_al_falaq_3.transliteration: Qul aʿūdhu birabbil-falaq. Min sharri mā khalaq. Wa min sharri ghāsiqin idhā waqab. Wa min sharrin-naffāthāti fil-ʿuqad. Wa min sharri ḥāsidin idhā ḥasad.
adhkar_al_falaq_3.purposeEn: Together with Al-Ikhlas and An-Nas, reciting this three times in the morning is reported to suffice as protection against everything.
adhkar_al_falaq_3.eveningPurposeEn: Together with Al-Ikhlas and An-Nas, reciting this three times in the evening is reported to suffice as protection against everything.
sources: Hisn al-Muslim 76; Qur’an 113:1-5; Abu Dawud 4/322; at-Tirmidhi 5/567
Hisn al-Muslim gives Al-Ikhlas, Al-Falaq and An-Nas as three recitations each in the morning and evening and cites Al-Albani’s Sahih at-Tirmidhi.

adhkar_an_nas_3.title: Surah An-Nas
adhkar_an_nas_3.arabic: قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ النَّاسِ, مَلِكِ النَّاسِ, إِلَٰهِ النَّاسِ, مِنْ شَرِّ الْوَسْوَاسِ الْخَنَّاسِ, الَّذِي يُوَسْوِسُ فِي صُدُورِ النَّاسِ, مِنَ الْجِنَّةِ وَالنَّاسِ
adhkar_an_nas_3.meaningEn: Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind, the King of mankind, the God of mankind, from the evil of the retreating whisperer who whispers into the hearts of mankind, from among jinn and mankind.
adhkar_an_nas_3.transliteration: Qul aʿūdhu birabbin-nās. Malikin-nās. Ilāhin-nās. Min sharril-waswāsil-khannās. Alladhī yuwaswisu fī ṣudūrin-nās. Minal-jinnati wan-nās.
adhkar_an_nas_3.purposeEn: Together with Al-Ikhlas and Al-Falaq, reciting this three times in the morning is reported to suffice as protection against everything.
adhkar_an_nas_3.eveningPurposeEn: Together with Al-Ikhlas and Al-Falaq, reciting this three times in the evening is reported to suffice as protection against everything.
sources: Hisn al-Muslim 76; Qur’an 114:1-6; Abu Dawud 4/322; at-Tirmidhi 5/567
Hisn al-Muslim gives Al-Ikhlas, Al-Falaq and An-Nas as three recitations each in the morning and evening and cites Al-Albani’s Sahih at-Tirmidhi.

adhkar_asbahna_amsayna_lillah.title: The Dominion Belongs to Allah
adhkar_asbahna_amsayna_lillah.arabic: أَصْبَحْنَا وَأَصْبَحَ الْمُلْكُ لِلَّهِ وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ، رَبِّ أَسْأَلُكَ خَيْرَ مَا فِي هَذَا الْيَوْمِ وَخَيْرَ مَا بَعْدَهُ، وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا فِي هَذَا الْيَوْمِ وَشَرِّ مَا بَعْدَهُ، رَبِّ أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ الْكَسَلِ وَسُوءِ الْكِبَرِ، رَبِّ أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ عَذَابٍ فِي النَّارِ وَعَذَابٍ فِي الْقَبْرِ
adhkar_asbahna_amsayna_lillah.eveningArabic: أَمْسَيْنَا وَأَمْسَى الْمُلْكُ لِلَّهِ وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ، رَبِّ أَسْأَلُكَ خَيْرَ مَا فِي هَذِهِ اللَّيْلَةِ وَخَيْرَ مَا بَعْدَهَا، وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا فِي هَذِهِ اللَّيْلَةِ وَشَرِّ مَا بَعْدَهَا، رَبِّ أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ الْكَسَلِ وَسُوءِ الْكِبَرِ، رَبِّ أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ عَذَابٍ فِي النَّارِ وَعَذَابٍ فِي الْقَبْرِ
adhkar_asbahna_amsayna_lillah.meaningEn: We have entered the morning and all dominion belongs to Allah. Praise is to Allah. None is worthy of worship except Allah alone, with no partner. His is the dominion and praise, and He is able to do all things. My Lord, I ask You for the good of this day and what follows it, and I seek refuge in You from its evil and the evil that follows it. I seek refuge in You from laziness, the misery of old age, the punishment of the Fire, and the punishment of the grave.
adhkar_asbahna_amsayna_lillah.eveningMeaningEn: We have entered the evening and all dominion belongs to Allah. Praise is to Allah. None is worthy of worship except Allah alone, with no partner. His is the dominion and praise, and He is able to do all things. My Lord, I ask You for the good of this night and what follows it, and I seek refuge in You from its evil and the evil that follows it. I seek refuge in You from laziness, the misery of old age, the punishment of the Fire, and the punishment of the grave.
adhkar_asbahna_amsayna_lillah.transliteration: Aṣbaḥnā wa aṣbaḥal-mulku lillāh, wal-ḥamdu lillāh, lā ilāha illallāhu waḥdahu lā sharīka lah, lahul-mulku wa lahul-ḥamd, wa huwa ʿalā kulli shay'in qadīr. Rabbi as'aluka khayra mā fī hādhā al-yawmi wa khayra mā baʿdahu, wa aʿūdhu bika min sharri mā fī hādhā al-yawmi wa sharri mā baʿdahu, Rabbi aʿūdhu bika minal-kasali wa sū'il-kibar, Rabbi aʿūdhu bika min ʿadhābin fin-nāri wa ʿadhābin fil-qabr.
adhkar_asbahna_amsayna_lillah.eveningTransliteration: Amsaynā wa amsal-mulku lillāh, wal-ḥamdu lillāh, lā ilāha illallāhu waḥdahu lā sharīka lah, lahul-mulku wa lahul-ḥamd, wa huwa ʿalā kulli shay'in qadīr. Rabbi as'aluka khayra mā fī hādhihil-laylati wa khayra mā baʿdahā, wa aʿūdhu bika min sharri mā fī hādhihil-laylati wa sharri mā baʿdahā, Rabbi aʿūdhu bika minal-kasali wa sū'il-kibar, Rabbi aʿūdhu bika min ʿadhābin fin-nāri wa ʿadhābin fil-qabr.
adhkar_asbahna_amsayna_lillah.purposeEn: Asks Allah for the goodness of the day and what follows, and seeks refuge from its evil, laziness, old age, Hellfire and grave punishment.
adhkar_asbahna_amsayna_lillah.eveningPurposeEn: Asks Allah for the goodness of the night and what follows, and seeks refuge from its evil, laziness, old age, Hellfire and grave punishment.
sources: Hisn al-Muslim 77; Sahih Muslim 4/2088
Recorded in Sahih Muslim. Hisn al-Muslim explicitly gives distinct day and night wording; the evening text uses “this night,” not “this day.”

adhkar_bika_asbahna_amsayna.title: By Allah We Enter Morning and Evening
adhkar_bika_asbahna_amsayna.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ بِكَ أَصْبَحْنَا وَبِكَ أَمْسَيْنَا وَبِكَ نَحْيَا وَبِكَ نَمُوتُ وَإِلَيْكَ النُّشُورُ
adhkar_bika_asbahna_amsayna.eveningArabic: اللَّهُمَّ بِكَ أَمْسَيْنَا وَبِكَ أَصْبَحْنَا وَبِكَ نَحْيَا وَبِكَ نَمُوتُ وَإِلَيْكَ الْمَصِيرُ
adhkar_bika_asbahna_amsayna.meaningEn: O Allah, by You we enter the morning and by You we enter the evening; by You we live and by You we die, and to You is the resurrection.
adhkar_bika_asbahna_amsayna.eveningMeaningEn: O Allah, by You we enter the evening and by You we enter the morning; by You we live and by You we die, and to You is the final return.
adhkar_bika_asbahna_amsayna.transliteration: Allāhumma bika aṣbaḥnā, wa bika amsaynā, wa bika naḥyā, wa bika namūtu, wa ilaykan-nushūr.
adhkar_bika_asbahna_amsayna.eveningTransliteration: Allāhumma bika amsaynā, wa bika aṣbaḥnā, wa bika naḥyā, wa bika namūtu, wa ilaykal-maṣīr.
adhkar_bika_asbahna_amsayna.purposeEn: Acknowledges that morning, evening, life, death and resurrection are by Allah.
adhkar_bika_asbahna_amsayna.eveningPurposeEn: Acknowledges that evening, morning, life, death and the final return are by Allah.
sources: Hisn al-Muslim 78; Al-Adab Al-Mufrad 1199; Abu Dawud 5068; at-Tirmidhi 3391
The transmitted wording varies across narrations. This app follows the Hisn al-Muslim 78 / Al-Adab Al-Mufrad wording: morning ends with an-nushur and evening with al-masir.

adhkar_sayyid_al_istighfar.title: Sayyid al-Istighfar
adhkar_sayyid_al_istighfar.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ رَبِّي لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ، خَلَقْتَنِي وَأَنَا عَبْدُكَ، وَأَنَا عَلَى عَهْدِكَ وَوَعْدِكَ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُ، أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا صَنَعْتُ، أَبُوءُ لَكَ بِنِعْمَتِكَ عَلَيَّ، وَأَبُوءُ بِذَنْبِي فَاغْفِرْ لِي فَإِنَّهُ لَا يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ
adhkar_sayyid_al_istighfar.meaningEn: O Allah, You are my Lord; none is worthy of worship except You. You created me and I am Your servant. I remain upon Your covenant and promise as much as I am able. I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I have done. I acknowledge Your favor upon me and acknowledge my sin, so forgive me; none forgives sins except You.
adhkar_sayyid_al_istighfar.transliteration: Allāhumma anta Rabbī lā ilāha illā ant, khalaqtanī wa anā ʿabduk, wa anā ʿalā ʿahdika wa waʿdika mastaṭaʿt, aʿūdhu bika min sharri mā ṣanaʿt, abū'u laka biniʿmatika ʿalayya, wa abū'u bidhanbī faghfir lī fa'innahu lā yaghfirudh-dhunūba illā ant.
adhkar_sayyid_al_istighfar.purposeEn: Master supplication for seeking forgiveness. Whoever says it in the morning with certainty and dies during that day is promised Paradise in the cited report.
adhkar_sayyid_al_istighfar.eveningPurposeEn: Master supplication for seeking forgiveness. Whoever says it in the evening with certainty and dies during that night is promised Paradise in the cited report.
sources: Hisn al-Muslim 79; Sahih al-Bukhari 6306
The virtue is recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari. The Word documents mixed the morning/day and evening/night statements; they are separated here.

adhkar_witness_tawhid_messenger_4.title: Witnessing Allah’s Oneness and the Messenger ﷺ
adhkar_witness_tawhid_messenger_4.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَصْبَحْتُ أُشْهِدُكَ وَأُشْهِدُ حَمَلَةَ عَرْشِكَ، وَمَلَائِكَتَكَ وَجَمِيعَ خَلْقِكَ، أَنَّكَ أَنْتَ اللَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ وَحْدَكَ لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ، وَأَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا عَبْدُكَ وَرَسُولُكَ
adhkar_witness_tawhid_messenger_4.eveningArabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَمْسَيْتُ أُشْهِدُكَ وَأُشْهِدُ حَمَلَةَ عَرْشِكَ، وَمَلَائِكَتَكَ وَجَمِيعَ خَلْقِكَ، أَنَّكَ أَنْتَ اللَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ وَحْدَكَ لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ، وَأَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا عَبْدُكَ وَرَسُولُكَ
adhkar_witness_tawhid_messenger_4.meaningEn: O Allah, I have entered the morning calling You, the bearers of Your Throne, Your angels and all creation to witness that You are Allah, none is worthy of worship except You alone with no partner, and Muhammad is Your servant and Messenger.
adhkar_witness_tawhid_messenger_4.eveningMeaningEn: O Allah, I have entered the evening calling You, the bearers of Your Throne, Your angels and all creation to witness that You are Allah, none is worthy of worship except You alone with no partner, and Muhammad is Your servant and Messenger.
adhkar_witness_tawhid_messenger_4.transliteration: Allāhumma innī aṣbaḥtu ush-hiduka wa ush-hidu ḥamalata ʿarshik, wa malā'ikataka wa jamīʿa khalqik, annaka antallāhu lā ilāha illā ant, waḥdaka lā sharīka lak, wa anna Muḥammadan ʿabduka wa rasūluk.
adhkar_witness_tawhid_messenger_4.eveningTransliteration: Allāhumma innī amsaytu ush-hiduka wa ush-hidu ḥamalata ʿarshik, wa malā'ikataka wa jamīʿa khalqik, annaka antallāhu lā ilāha illā ant, waḥdaka lā sharīka lak, wa anna Muḥammadan ʿabduka wa rasūluk.
adhkar_witness_tawhid_messenger_4.purposeEn: Declares Allah’s oneness and Muhammad ﷺ as His servant and Messenger. The cited report links four recitations with being spared from the Fire.
adhkar_witness_tawhid_messenger_4.eveningPurposeEn: Declares Allah’s oneness and Muhammad ﷺ as His servant and Messenger. The cited report links four recitations with being spared from the Fire.
sources: Hisn al-Muslim 80; Abu Dawud 4/317 (5069); Al-Adab Al-Mufrad 1201; an-Nasa’i, ‘Amal al-Yawm wal-Laylah 9 (as-Sunan al-Kubra 9753); Ibn as-Sunni 70

Hisn al-Muslim cites the Abu Dawud and an-Nasa’i chains as Hasan and specifies four repetitions morning or evening. A current Sunnah.com page for Abu Dawud 5069 separately lists Al-Albani’s grading as Da‘if, so the grading difference is preserved rather than flattened into one app-level authenticity claim. An-Nawawi called Abu Dawud’s chain good (jayyid), Ibn Hajar called the hadith Hasan Gharib, and Ibn Baz graded it Hasan. Wording note: this entry follows Hisn al-Muslim 80, which includes waḥdaka lā sharīka lak (alone, with no partner); those words are in Al-Adab Al-Mufrad 1201 and an-Nasa’i’s as-Sunan al-Kubra 9753, but not in the text of Abu Dawud 5069.

adhkar_blessings_gratitude.title: Gratitude for Allah’s Blessings
adhkar_blessings_gratitude.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ مَا أَصْبَحَ بِي مِنْ نِعْمَةٍ أَوْ بِأَحَدٍ مِنْ خَلْقِكَ، فَمِنْكَ وَحْدَكَ لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ، فَلَكَ الْحَمْدُ وَلَكَ الشُّكْرُ
adhkar_blessings_gratitude.eveningArabic: اللَّهُمَّ مَا أَمْسَى بِي مِنْ نِعْمَةٍ أَوْ بِأَحَدٍ مِنْ خَلْقِكَ، فَمِنْكَ وَحْدَكَ لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ، فَلَكَ الْحَمْدُ وَلَكَ الشُّكْرُ
adhkar_blessings_gratitude.meaningEn: O Allah, every blessing that I or any of Your creation have received this morning is from You alone, with no partner. To You belong all praise and thanks.
adhkar_blessings_gratitude.eveningMeaningEn: O Allah, every blessing that I or any of Your creation have received this evening is from You alone, with no partner. To You belong all praise and thanks.
adhkar_blessings_gratitude.transliteration: Allāhumma mā aṣbaḥa bī min niʿmatin aw bi-aḥadin min khalqik, fa minka waḥdaka lā sharīka lak, falakal-ḥamdu wa lakash-shukr.
adhkar_blessings_gratitude.eveningTransliteration: Allāhumma mā amsā bī min niʿmatin aw bi-aḥadin min khalqik, fa minka waḥdaka lā sharīka lak, falakal-ḥamdu wa lakash-shukr.
adhkar_blessings_gratitude.purposeEn: Expresses gratitude to Allah for every blessing; the cited report says it completes one’s gratitude for that day.
adhkar_blessings_gratitude.eveningPurposeEn: Expresses gratitude to Allah for every blessing; the cited report says it completes one’s gratitude for that night.
sources: Hisn al-Muslim 81; Abu Dawud 4/318; an-Nasa’i; Ibn as-Sunni 41; Ibn Hibban 2361
Hisn al-Muslim cites the chain as Hasan and gives distinct morning (asbaha) and evening (amsa) wording.

adhkar_health_hearing_sight_3.title: Wellbeing in Body, Hearing, and Sight
adhkar_health_hearing_sight_3.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ عَافِنِي فِي بَدَنِي، اللَّهُمَّ عَافِنِي فِي سَمْعِي، اللَّهُمَّ عَافِنِي فِي بَصَرِي، لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ. اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ الْكُفْرِ وَالْفَقْرِ، وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ عَذَابِ الْقَبْرِ، لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ
adhkar_health_hearing_sight_3.meaningEn: O Allah, grant me wellbeing in my body, preserve my hearing and preserve my sight. None is worthy of worship except You. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from disbelief and poverty, and from the punishment of the grave. None is worthy of worship except You.
adhkar_health_hearing_sight_3.transliteration: Allāhumma ʿāfinī fī badanī, Allāhumma ʿāfinī fī samʿī, Allāhumma ʿāfinī fī baṣarī, lā ilāha illā ant. Allāhumma innī aʿūdhu bika minal-kufri wal-faqri, wa aʿūdhu bika min ʿadhābil-qabri, lā ilāha illā ant.
adhkar_health_hearing_sight_3.purposeEn: Asks Allah for bodily wellbeing and preservation of hearing and sight, and seeks refuge from disbelief, poverty and grave punishment.
sources: Hisn al-Muslim 82; Abu Dawud 4/324; Ahmad 5/42; an-Nasa’i; Ibn as-Sunni 69
Hisn al-Muslim cites the chain as Hasan and specifies three repetitions.

adhkar_hasbiyallahu_7.title: Allah Is Sufficient for Me
adhkar_hasbiyallahu_7.arabic: حَسْبِيَ اللَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ، عَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ، وَهُوَ رَبُّ الْعَرْشِ الْعَظِيمِ
adhkar_hasbiyallahu_7.meaningEn: Allah is sufficient for me. None is worthy of worship except Him. I place my trust in Him, and He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne.
adhkar_hasbiyallahu_7.transliteration: Ḥasbiyallāhu lā ilāha illā huwa, ʿalayhi tawakkaltu, wa huwa Rabbul-ʿArshil-ʿAẓīm.
adhkar_hasbiyallahu_7.purposeEn: Affirms reliance upon Allah. Hisn al-Muslim reports that seven recitations morning or evening are linked with Allah sufficing the person in what concerns them.
sources: Hisn al-Muslim 83; Ibn as-Sunni 71; Abu Dawud 4/321
Hisn al-Muslim presents the report as sound (Sahih) and prescribes seven repetitions morning or evening.

adhkar_afw_afiyah.title: Forgiveness and Wellbeing
adhkar_afw_afiyah.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ الْعَفْوَ وَالْعَافِيَةَ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ، اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ الْعَفْوَ وَالْعَافِيَةَ فِي دِينِي وَدُنْيَايَ وَأَهْلِي وَمَالِي، اللَّهُمَّ اسْتُرْ عَوْرَاتِي وَآمِنْ رَوْعَاتِي، اللَّهُمَّ احْفَظْنِي مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيَّ وَمِنْ خَلْفِي وَعَنْ يَمِينِي وَعَنْ شِمَالِي وَمِنْ فَوْقِي، وَأَعُوذُ بِعَظَمَتِكَ أَنْ أُغْتَالَ مِنْ تَحْتِي
adhkar_afw_afiyah.meaningEn: O Allah, I ask You for forgiveness and wellbeing in this world and the Hereafter, in my religion, worldly affairs, family and wealth. Conceal my faults and calm my fears. Guard me from before me, behind me, my right, my left and above me; I seek refuge in Your greatness from being taken from beneath me.
adhkar_afw_afiyah.transliteration: Allāhumma innī as'alukal-ʿafwa wal-ʿāfiyata fid-dunyā wal-ākhirah. Allāhumma innī as'alukal-ʿafwa wal-ʿāfiyata fī dīnī wa dunyāya wa ahlī wa mālī. Allāhumma-stur ʿawrātī wa āmin rawʿātī. Allāhumma iḥfaẓnī min bayni yadayya wa min khalfī wa ʿan yamīnī wa ʿan shimālī wa min fawqī, wa aʿūdhu biʿaẓamatika an ughtāla min taḥtī.
adhkar_afw_afiyah.purposeEn: Asks Allah for forgiveness, wellbeing, safety for religion, family and wealth, concealment of faults and protection from every direction.
sources: Hisn al-Muslim 84; Sahih Ibn Majah 2/332; Abu Dawud
Hisn al-Muslim cites Sahih Ibn Majah and Abu Dawud for this morning/evening supplication.

adhkar_knower_unseen_refuge.title: Refuge from the Evil of the Self and Satan
adhkar_knower_unseen_refuge.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ عَالِمَ الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهَادَةِ، فَاطِرَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ، رَبَّ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَمَلِيكَهُ، أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ، أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ نَفْسِي، وَمِنْ شَرِّ الشَّيْطَانِ وَشِرْكِهِ، وَأَنْ أَقْتَرِفَ عَلَى نَفْسِي سُوءًا أَوْ أَجُرَّهُ إِلَى مُسْلِمٍ
adhkar_knower_unseen_refuge.meaningEn: O Allah, Knower of the unseen and the seen, Creator of the heavens and earth, Lord and Sovereign of everything, I testify that none is worthy of worship except You. I seek refuge in You from the evil of myself and from the evil and shirk of Satan, and from committing evil against myself or bringing it upon another Muslim.
adhkar_knower_unseen_refuge.transliteration: Allāhumma ʿālimal-ghaybi wash-shahādati fāṭiras-samāwāti wal-arḍ, Rabba kulli shay'in wa malīkah, ash-hadu an lā ilāha illā ant, aʿūdhu bika min sharri nafsī, wa min sharrish-shayṭāni wa shirkih, wa an aqtarifa ʿalā nafsī sū'an aw ajurrahu ilā Muslim.
adhkar_knower_unseen_refuge.purposeEn: Seeks protection from the evil of one’s own soul, Satan, shirk, self-harm through sin, and harming another Muslim.
sources: Hisn al-Muslim 85; Sahih at-Tirmidhi 3/142; Abu Dawud
Hisn al-Muslim cites Sahih at-Tirmidhi and Abu Dawud for this morning/evening supplication.

adhkar_bismillah_alladhi_3.title: Protection in Allah’s Name
adhkar_bismillah_alladhi_3.arabic: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الَّذِي لَا يَضُرُّ مَعَ اسْمِهِ شَيْءٌ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلَا فِي السَّمَاءِ وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ
adhkar_bismillah_alladhi_3.meaningEn: In the name of Allah, with whose name nothing on earth or in heaven can cause harm, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
adhkar_bismillah_alladhi_3.transliteration: Bismillāhil-ladhī lā yaḍurru maʿasmihi shay'un fil-arḍi wa lā fis-samā'i wa huwas-Samīʿul-ʿAlīm.
adhkar_bismillah_alladhi_3.purposeEn: The cited report says that saying this three times in the morning protects from sudden calamity until evening.
adhkar_bismillah_alladhi_3.eveningPurposeEn: The cited report says that saying this three times in the evening protects from sudden calamity until morning.
sources: Hisn al-Muslim 86; Abu Dawud 4/323; at-Tirmidhi 5/465; Ibn Majah 2/332; Ahmad
Hisn al-Muslim specifies three repetitions and cites a Hasan chain; the app keeps the morning and evening protection windows separate.

adhkar_raditu_billahi_3.title: Contentment with Allah, Islam, and the Prophet ﷺ
adhkar_raditu_billahi_3.arabic: رَضِيتُ بِاللَّهِ رَبًّا، وَبِالْإِسْلَامِ دِينًا، وَبِمُحَمَّدٍ نَبِيًّا
adhkar_raditu_billahi_3.meaningEn: I am pleased with Allah as my Lord, Islam as my religion, and Muhammad ﷺ as my Prophet.
adhkar_raditu_billahi_3.transliteration: Raḍītu billāhi Rabban, wa bil-Islāmi dīnan, wa bi-Muḥammadin Nabiyyan.
adhkar_raditu_billahi_3.purposeEn: Expresses contentment with Allah, Islam and the Prophet ﷺ. The cited report says that whoever says it three times every morning or evening will be pleased on the Day of Resurrection.
sources: Hisn al-Muslim 87; Ahmad 4/337; an-Nasa’i; Ibn as-Sunni 68; at-Tirmidhi 5/465
Hisn al-Muslim cites the chain as Hasan and specifies three repetitions every morning or evening.

adhkar_ya_hayyu_ya_qayyum.title: O Ever-Living, O Sustainer
adhkar_ya_hayyu_ya_qayyum.arabic: يَا حَيُّ يَا قَيُّومُ، بِرَحْمَتِكَ أَسْتَغِيثُ، أَصْلِحْ لِي شَأْنِي كُلَّهُ، وَلَا تَكِلْنِي إِلَى نَفْسِي طَرْفَةَ عَيْنٍ
adhkar_ya_hayyu_ya_qayyum.meaningEn: O Ever-Living, O Sustainer, by Your mercy I seek help. Set right all of my affairs and do not leave me to myself even for the blink of an eye.
adhkar_ya_hayyu_ya_qayyum.transliteration: Yā Ḥayyu yā Qayyūmu, biraḥmatika astaghīthu, aṣliḥ lī sha’nī kullahu, wa lā takilnī ilā nafsī ṭarfata ʿayn.
adhkar_ya_hayyu_ya_qayyum.purposeEn: Seeks Allah’s mercy and help to set all affairs right and not leave the person to their own self even momentarily.
sources: Hisn al-Muslim 88; Al-Hakim 1/545; Sahih at-Targhib wa at-Tarhib 1/273
Hisn al-Muslim states that the chain is sound (Sahih).

adhkar_good_of_day_night.title: Goodness, Victory, Light, Blessing, and Guidance
adhkar_good_of_day_night.arabic: أَصْبَحْنَا وَأَصْبَحَ الْمُلْكُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ، اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ خَيْرَ هَذَا الْيَوْمِ، فَتْحَهُ وَنَصْرَهُ وَنُورَهُ وَبَرَكَتَهُ وَهُدَاهُ، وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا فِيهِ وَشَرِّ مَا بَعْدَهُ
adhkar_good_of_day_night.eveningArabic: أَمْسَيْنَا وَأَمْسَى الْمُلْكُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ، اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ خَيْرَ هَذِهِ اللَّيْلَةِ، فَتْحَهَا وَنَصْرَهَا وَنُورَهَا وَبَرَكَتَهَا وَهُدَاهَا، وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا فِيهَا وَشَرِّ مَا بَعْدَهَا
adhkar_good_of_day_night.meaningEn: We have entered the morning and all dominion belongs to Allah, Lord of all worlds. O Allah, I ask You for the goodness of this day—its opening, victory, light, blessing and guidance—and I seek refuge in You from the evil within it and the evil that follows it.
adhkar_good_of_day_night.eveningMeaningEn: We have entered the evening and all dominion belongs to Allah, Lord of all worlds. O Allah, I ask You for the goodness of this night—its opening, victory, light, blessing and guidance—and I seek refuge in You from the evil within it and the evil that follows it.
adhkar_good_of_day_night.transliteration: Aṣbaḥnā wa aṣbaḥal-mulku lillāhi Rabbil-ʿālamīn. Allāhumma innī as'aluka khayra hādhā al-yawm: fatḥahu wa naṣrahu wa nūrahu wa barakatahu wa hudāhu, wa aʿūdhu bika min sharri mā fīhi wa sharri mā baʿdahu.
adhkar_good_of_day_night.eveningTransliteration: Amsaynā wa amsal-mulku lillāhi Rabbil-ʿālamīn. Allāhumma innī as'aluka khayra hādhihil-laylah: fatḥahā wa naṣrahā wa nūrahā wa barakatahā wa hudāhā, wa aʿūdhu bika min sharri mā fīhā wa sharri mā baʿdahā.
adhkar_good_of_day_night.purposeEn: Asks Allah for the goodness, victory, help, light, blessing and guidance of the day, and refuge from its evil.
adhkar_good_of_day_night.eveningPurposeEn: Asks Allah for the goodness, victory, help, light, blessing and guidance of the night, and refuge from its evil.
sources: Hisn al-Muslim 89; Abu Dawud 4/322
Hisn al-Muslim cites the chain as Hasan. The Evening document incorrectly retained “day” wording in places; the verified evening version uses “this night.”

adhkar_fitrah_islam.title: Upon the Fitrah of Islam
adhkar_fitrah_islam.arabic: أَصْبَحْنَا عَلَى فِطْرَةِ الْإِسْلَامِ، وَعَلَى كَلِمَةِ الْإِخْلَاصِ، وَعَلَى دِينِ نَبِيِّنَا مُحَمَّدٍ، وَعَلَى مِلَّةِ أَبِينَا إِبْرَاهِيمَ حَنِيفًا مُسْلِمًا وَمَا كَانَ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ
adhkar_fitrah_islam.eveningArabic: أَمْسَيْنَا عَلَى فِطْرَةِ الْإِسْلَامِ، وَعَلَى كَلِمَةِ الْإِخْلَاصِ، وَعَلَى دِينِ نَبِيِّنَا مُحَمَّدٍ، وَعَلَى مِلَّةِ أَبِينَا إِبْرَاهِيمَ حَنِيفًا مُسْلِمًا وَمَا كَانَ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ
adhkar_fitrah_islam.meaningEn: We have entered the morning upon the natural religion of Islam, the word of sincere devotion, the religion of our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, and the way of our father Ibrahim, upright and Muslim, who was not among the polytheists.
adhkar_fitrah_islam.eveningMeaningEn: We have entered the evening upon the natural religion of Islam, the word of sincere devotion, the religion of our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, and the way of our father Ibrahim, upright and Muslim, who was not among the polytheists.
adhkar_fitrah_islam.transliteration: Aṣbaḥnā ʿalā fiṭratil-Islām, wa ʿalā kalimatil-ikhlāṣ, wa ʿalā dīni nabiyyinā Muḥammadin, wa ʿalā millati abīnā Ibrāhīma, ḥanīfan Musliman wa mā kāna minal-mushrikīn.
adhkar_fitrah_islam.eveningTransliteration: Amsaynā ʿalā fiṭratil-Islām, wa ʿalā kalimatil-ikhlāṣ, wa ʿalā dīni nabiyyinā Muḥammadin, wa ʿalā millati abīnā Ibrāhīma, ḥanīfan Musliman wa mā kāna minal-mushrikīn.
adhkar_fitrah_islam.purposeEn: Renews affirmation of the fitrah of Islam, sincere devotion, the religion of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and the upright way of Ibrahim عليه السلام.
sources: Hisn al-Muslim 90; Ahmad 3/406-407 and 5/123; an-Nasa’i; at-Tirmidhi 4/209
Hisn al-Muslim gives distinct morning “asbahna” and evening “amsayna” openings. No additional grading claim is added beyond the cited collection references.

adhkar_subhanallah_wabihamdihi_100.title: SubhanAllahi wa Bihamdihi
adhkar_subhanallah_wabihamdihi_100.meaningEn: Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him.
adhkar_subhanallah_wabihamdihi_100.purposeEn: A dhikr of glorification and praise. The authentic report says that one hundred repetitions in the morning and evening have exceptional merit on the Day of Resurrection.
sources: Hisn al-Muslim 91; Sahih Muslim 2692
Sahih Muslim 2692 explicitly states one hundred times in the morning and one hundred times in the evening.

adhkar_tahlil_10.title: La Ilaha Illallah Wahdahu — 10 Times
adhkar_tahlil_10.arabic: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ، وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
adhkar_tahlil_10.meaningEn: None has the right to be worshipped except Allah, alone, without partner, to Him belongs all sovereignty and praise, and He is over all things omnipotent.
adhkar_tahlil_10.transliteration: Lā ilāha illallāhu waḥdahu lā sharīka lah, lahul-mulku wa lahul-ḥamdu, wa huwa ʿalā kulli shay'in qadīr.
adhkar_tahlil_10.purposeEn: Hisn al-Muslim lists this tahlil among the adhkar of the morning and the evening.
adhkar_tahlil_10.practiceEn: Say it ten times, or once when feeling lazy.
sources: Hisn al-Muslim 92

Arabic and English meaning copied from Hisn al-Muslim (hisnmuslim.com, Morning and Evening chapter): ten times in the morning and the evening, or once when feeling lazy. The hadith references in its footnote were not re-checked in the app and need scholarly confirmation.

adhkar_tahlil_100_morning.title: La Ilaha Illallah Wahdahu — 100 Times
adhkar_tahlil_100_morning.arabic: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ، وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
adhkar_tahlil_100_morning.meaningEn: None is worthy of worship except Allah alone, with no partner. His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He is able to do all things.
adhkar_tahlil_100_morning.transliteration: Lā ilāha illallāhu waḥdahu lā sharīka lah, lahul-mulku wa lahul-ḥamdu, wa huwa ʿalā kulli shay'in qadīr.
adhkar_tahlil_100_morning.purposeEn: The cited authentic report gives the reward of freeing ten slaves, one hundred good deeds, removal of one hundred bad deeds, and protection from Satan until evening for one hundred repetitions in a day; Hisn al-Muslim places this as a morning recitation.
sources: Hisn al-Muslim 93; Sahih al-Bukhari 6403; Sahih Muslim 2691
Hisn al-Muslim specifies 100 times upon rising in the morning. The Word document’s evening copy of this item is removed because the cited Hisn entry is morning-specific.

adhkar_subhanallah_creation_3_morning.title: Praise by the Number of Allah’s Creation
adhkar_subhanallah_creation_3_morning.arabic: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ، عَدَدَ خَلْقِهِ، وَرِضَا نَفْسِهِ، وَزِنَةَ عَرْشِهِ، وَمِدَادَ كَلِمَاتِهِ
adhkar_subhanallah_creation_3_morning.meaningEn: Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him, by the number of His creation, by His pleasure, by the weight of His Throne, and by the extent of His words.
adhkar_subhanallah_creation_3_morning.transliteration: Subḥānallāhi wa biḥamdih, ʿadada khalqih, wa riḍā nafsih, wa zinata ʿarshih, wa midāda kalimātih.
adhkar_subhanallah_creation_3_morning.purposeEn: A morning glorification and praise of Allah using these four expressions of abundance.
sources: Hisn al-Muslim 94; Sahih Muslim 4/2090
Hisn al-Muslim specifies three repetitions upon rising in the morning. It is therefore not included in the Evening list.

adhkar_beneficial_knowledge_morning.title: Beneficial Knowledge, Good Provision, Accepted Deeds
adhkar_beneficial_knowledge_morning.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ عِلْمًا نَافِعًا، وَرِزْقًا طَيِّبًا، وَعَمَلًا مُتَقَبَّلًا
adhkar_beneficial_knowledge_morning.meaningEn: O Allah, I ask You for beneficial knowledge, good provision, and accepted deeds.
adhkar_beneficial_knowledge_morning.transliteration: Allāhumma innī as’aluka ʿilman nāfiʿan, wa rizqan ṭayyiban, wa ʿamalan mutaqabbalan.
adhkar_beneficial_knowledge_morning.purposeEn: A supplication after the Fajr prayer asking Allah for beneficial knowledge, wholesome provision, and accepted deeds.
sources: Hisn al-Muslim 95; Sunan Ibn Majah 925
Sunan Ibn Majah 925 records this after the Subh/Fajr prayer and is graded Sahih (Darussalam). It is not an evening dhikr.

adhkar_astaghfirullah_100_daytime.title: Seeking Forgiveness and Repenting
adhkar_astaghfirullah_100_daytime.meaningEn: I seek Allah’s forgiveness and repent to Him.
adhkar_astaghfirullah_100_daytime.purposeEn: Seeking forgiveness and repentance. The cited source says one hundred times during the day; it is not specifically an evening adhkar item.
sources: Hisn al-Muslim 96; Sahih al-Bukhari; Sahih Muslim 4/2075

Hisn al-Muslim specifies one hundred times during the day. It remains in the Morning document’s sequence for this feature, but its timing is explicitly labeled “during the day” and it is removed from the Evening list.

adhkar_perfect_words_evening_3.title: Refuge in Allah’s Perfect Words
adhkar_perfect_words_evening_3.arabic: أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّاتِ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ
adhkar_perfect_words_evening_3.meaningEn: I seek refuge in the Perfect Words of Allah from the evil of what He has created.
adhkar_perfect_words_evening_3.transliteration: Aʿūdhu bikalimātillāhit-tāmmāti min sharri mā khalaq.
adhkar_perfect_words_evening_3.purposeEn: The cited report states that saying this three times in the evening protects from insect stings.
sources: Hisn al-Muslim 97; Ahmad 2/290; an-Nasa’i, Amalul-Yawm wal-Laylah 590; at-Tirmidhi 3/187; Ibn as-Sunni 68; Ibn Majah 2/266

Hisn al-Muslim specifies three repetitions in the evening. It reports Al-Albani grading the Ibn Majah chain Sahih and notes the at-Tirmidhi report as Hasan. The Morning Word document incorrectly places this as a morning item, so it is shown only under Evening.

adhkar_salawat_10.title: Sending Blessings upon the Prophet ﷺ
adhkar_salawat_10.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ وَسَلِّمْ عَلَى نَبِيِّنَا مُحَمَّدٍ
adhkar_salawat_10.meaningEn: O Allah, send Your blessings and peace upon our Prophet Muhammad.
adhkar_salawat_10.transliteration: Allāhumma ṣalli wa sallim ʿalā nabiyyinā Muḥammad.
adhkar_salawat_10.purposeEn: Sends blessings and peace upon the Prophet ﷺ. The cited report links ten recitations in the morning and ten in the evening with his intercession on the Day of Resurrection.
sources: Hisn al-Muslim 98; at-Tabarani; Majmaʿ az-Zawa’id 10/120; Sahih at-Targhib wa at-Tarhib 1/273
Hisn al-Muslim reports two chains from at-Tabarani and describes one as reliable (Jayyid). The app preserves that attribution rather than relabeling it as an independent app-level grading.

prophetic_distress.title: At a Time of Distress
prophetic_distress.arabic: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ الْعَظِيمُ الْحَلِيمُ، لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ رَبُّ الْعَرْشِ الْعَظِيمِ، لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ رَبُّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَرَبُّ الْأَرْضِ، وَرَبُّ الْعَرْشِ الْكَرِيمِ
prophetic_distress.meaningEn: There is none worthy of worship except Allah, the Magnificent, the Forbearing; none worthy of worship except Allah, Lord of the Mighty Throne; none worthy of worship except Allah, Lord of the heavens, Lord of the earth, and Lord of the Noble Throne.
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 6346; Sahih Muslim 2730
Recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim as a supplication said at a time of distress.

prophetic_debt_before_sleep.title: Relief from Debt and Poverty
prophetic_debt_before_sleep.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ رَبَّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَرَبَّ الْأَرْضِ وَرَبَّ الْعَرْشِ الْعَظِيمِ، رَبَّنَا وَرَبَّ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ، فَالِقَ الْحَبِّ وَالنَّوَى، وَمُنْزِلَ التَّوْرَاةِ وَالْإِنْجِيلِ وَالْفُرْقَانِ، أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ أَنْتَ آخِذٌ بِنَاصِيَتِهِ، أَنْتَ الْأَوَّلُ فَلَيْسَ قَبْلَكَ شَيْءٌ، وَأَنْتَ الْآخِرُ فَلَيْسَ بَعْدَكَ شَيْءٌ، وَأَنْتَ الظَّاهِرُ فَلَيْسَ فَوْقَكَ شَيْءٌ، وَأَنْتَ الْبَاطِنُ فَلَيْسَ دُونَكَ شَيْءٌ، اقْضِ عَنَّا الدَّيْنَ وَأَغْنِنَا مِنَ الْفَقْرِ
prophetic_debt_before_sleep.meaningEn: O Allah, Lord of the heavens, the earth, and the Mighty Throne; our Lord and Lord of everything; Splitter of the grain and date-stone; Revealer of the Torah, Gospel, and Criterion: I seek refuge in You from the evil of everything under Your control. You are the First and nothing is before You; You are the Last and nothing is after You; You are the Manifest and nothing is above You; You are the Hidden and nothing is beyond You. Settle our debt and enrich us from poverty.
sources: Sahih Muslim 2713
Recorded in Sahih Muslim in the context of the supplication said when going to sleep.

prophetic_quran_spring_heart.title: The Quran as the Spring of the Heart
prophetic_quran_spring_heart.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي عَبْدُكَ، ابْنُ عَبْدِكَ، ابْنُ أَمَتِكَ، نَاصِيَتِي بِيَدِكَ، مَاضٍ فِيَّ حُكْمُكَ، عَدْلٌ فِيَّ قَضَاؤُكَ، أَسْأَلُكَ بِكُلِّ اسْمٍ هُوَ لَكَ سَمَّيْتَ بِهِ نَفْسَكَ، أَوْ عَلَّمْتَهُ أَحَدًا مِنْ خَلْقِكَ، أَوْ أَنْزَلْتَهُ فِي كِتَابِكَ، أَوِ اسْتَأْثَرْتَ بِهِ فِي عِلْمِ الْغَيْبِ عِنْدَكَ، أَنْ تَجْعَلَ الْقُرْآنَ رَبِيعَ قَلْبِي، وَنُورَ صَدْرِي، وَجَلَاءَ حُزْنِي، وَذَهَابَ هَمِّي
prophetic_quran_spring_heart.meaningEn: O Allah, I am Your servant, son of Your servant, son of Your female servant. My forelock is in Your hand; Your judgment over me is carried out and Your decree concerning me is just. I ask You by every name that is Yours—by which You named Yourself, taught any of Your creation, revealed in Your Book, or kept with Yourself in the knowledge of the unseen—to make the Quran the spring of my heart, the light of my chest, the removal of my sadness, and the departure of my worry.
sources: Musnad Ahmad 3712; Sahih Ibn Hibban 972

The report has been authenticated by a number of hadith scholars, while assessments of individual chains and some transmitted wording differ. This entry preserves the corrected source document’s Ahmad wording rather than flattening those differences. Wording note: Musnad Ahmad 3712 and al-Albani's as-Silsilah as-Sahihah 199 read nūra ṣadrī (the light of my chest), as shown here, while Sahih Ibn Hibban 972 reads nūra baṣarī (the light of my sight). Shuʿayb al-Arnaʾut graded Ahmad's chain weak and Ibn Hibban's report Sahih; al-Albani graded the hadith Sahih.

prophetic_soul_piety.title: Piety and Purification of the Soul
prophetic_soul_piety.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ آتِ نَفْسِي تَقْوَاهَا، وَزَكِّهَا أَنْتَ خَيْرُ مَنْ زَكَّاهَا، أَنْتَ وَلِيُّهَا وَمَوْلَاهَا
prophetic_soul_piety.meaningEn: O Allah, grant my soul its piety and purify it; You are the best to purify it. You are its Protecting Friend and Master.
sources: Sahih Muslim 2722
Recorded in Sahih Muslim.

prophetic_beneficial_knowledge.title: Beneficial Knowledge
prophetic_beneficial_knowledge.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ انْفَعْنِي بِمَا عَلَّمْتَنِي، وَعَلِّمْنِي مَا يَنْفَعُنِي، وَزِدْنِي عِلْمًا
prophetic_beneficial_knowledge.meaningEn: O Allah, benefit me with what You have taught me, teach me what will benefit me, and increase me in knowledge.
sources: Jami‘ at-Tirmidhi 3599; Sunan Ibn Majah 3833

Grading differs across editions and scholars. Sunnah.com’s Darussalam display grades these particular routes Da‘if, while al-Albani authenticated the short core wording through other analysis/routes and excluded or qualified some longer additions. The app therefore preserves the short core wording and does not label the entry unconditionally Sahih.

prophetic_comprehensive_help.title: Help, Guidance, Gratitude, and Repentance
prophetic_comprehensive_help.arabic: رَبِّ أَعِنِّي وَلَا تُعِنْ عَلَيَّ، وَانْصُرْنِي وَلَا تَنْصُرْ عَلَيَّ، وَامْكُرْ لِي وَلَا تَمْكُرْ عَلَيَّ، وَاهْدِنِي وَيَسِّرِ الْهُدَى لِي، وَانْصُرْنِي عَلَى مَنْ بَغَى عَلَيَّ، رَبِّ اجْعَلْنِي لَكَ شَكَّارًا، لَكَ ذَكَّارًا، لَكَ رَهَّابًا، لَكَ مِطْوَاعًا، لَكَ مُخْبِتًا، إِلَيْكَ أَوَّاهًا مُنِيبًا، رَبِّ تَقَبَّلْ تَوْبَتِي، وَاغْسِلْ حَوْبَتِي، وَأَجِبْ دَعْوَتِي، وَثَبِّتْ حُجَّتِي، وَسَدِّدْ لِسَانِي، وَاهْدِ قَلْبِي، وَاسْلُلْ سَخِيمَةَ صَدْرِي
prophetic_comprehensive_help.meaningEn: My Lord, help me and do not help against me; grant me victory and do not grant victory over me; plan for me and not against me; guide me and make guidance easy for me; and grant me victory over whoever transgresses against me. My Lord, make me grateful to You, remembering You, fearful of You, obedient to You, humble before You, often turning and returning to You. My Lord, accept my repentance, wash away my sin, answer my supplication, make my proof firm, make my tongue truthful and steady, guide my heart, and remove rancor from my chest.
sources: Jami‘ at-Tirmidhi 3551; Sunan Abi Dawud 1510
At-Tirmidhi described the report as Hasan Sahih; the cited Abu Dawud route is also authenticated in common contemporary grading.

prophetic_worry_grief_debt.title: Protection from Worry, Grief, Weakness, and Debt
prophetic_worry_grief_debt.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ الْهَمِّ وَالْحَزَنِ، وَالْعَجْزِ وَالْكَسَلِ، وَالْجُبْنِ وَالْبُخْلِ، وَضَلَعِ الدَّيْنِ وَغَلَبَةِ الرِّجَالِ
prophetic_worry_grief_debt.meaningEn: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from worry and grief, incapacity and laziness, cowardice and miserliness, the burden of debt, and being overpowered by people.
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 6369

Sahih al-Bukhari 6369 is the exact source for this wording. The corrected source document also listed Sahih Muslim 2706 as similar, but Muslim 2706 contains a related refuge supplication with materially different wording, so it is not presented here as an exact parallel reference.

prophetic_unbeneficial_knowledge.title: Protection from Unbeneficial Knowledge
prophetic_unbeneficial_knowledge.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ عِلْمٍ لَا يَنْفَعُ، وَمِنْ قَلْبٍ لَا يَخْشَعُ، وَمِنْ نَفْسٍ لَا تَشْبَعُ، وَمِنْ دَعْوَةٍ لَا يُسْتَجَابُ لَهَا
prophetic_unbeneficial_knowledge.meaningEn: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from knowledge that does not benefit, a heart that is not humble, a soul that is not satisfied, and a supplication that is not answered.
sources: Sahih Muslim 2722
Recorded in Sahih Muslim.

prophetic_refuge_pleasure.title: Seeking Refuge in Allah’s Pleasure and Pardon
prophetic_refuge_pleasure.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِرِضَاكَ مِنْ سَخَطِكَ، وَبِمُعَافَاتِكَ مِنْ عُقُوبَتِكَ، وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْكَ، لَا أُحْصِي ثَنَاءً عَلَيْكَ، أَنْتَ كَمَا أَثْنَيْتَ عَلَى نَفْسِكَ
prophetic_refuge_pleasure.meaningEn: O Allah, I seek refuge in Your pleasure from Your anger, in Your pardon from Your punishment, and I seek refuge in You from You. I cannot enumerate Your praise; You are as You have praised Yourself.
sources: Sahih Muslim 486
Recorded in Sahih Muslim in the context of prostration.

prophetic_all_good.title: All Good, Paradise, and a Good Decree
prophetic_all_good.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ مِنَ الْخَيْرِ كُلِّهِ عَاجِلِهِ وَآجِلِهِ، مَا عَلِمْتُ مِنْهُ وَمَا لَمْ أَعْلَمْ، وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ الشَّرِّ كُلِّهِ عَاجِلِهِ وَآجِلِهِ، مَا عَلِمْتُ مِنْهُ وَمَا لَمْ أَعْلَمْ، اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ مِنْ خَيْرِ مَا سَأَلَكَ عَبْدُكَ وَنَبِيُّكَ، وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا عَاذَ بِهِ عَبْدُكَ وَنَبِيُّكَ، اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ الْجَنَّةَ وَمَا قَرَّبَ إِلَيْهَا مِنْ قَوْلٍ أَوْ عَمَلٍ، وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ النَّارِ وَمَا قَرَّبَ إِلَيْهَا مِنْ قَوْلٍ أَوْ عَمَلٍ، وَأَسْأَلُكَ أَنْ تَجْعَلَ كُلَّ قَضَاءٍ قَضَيْتَهُ لِي خَيْرًا
prophetic_all_good.meaningEn: O Allah, I ask You for every good, immediate and later, what I know of it and what I do not know; and I seek refuge in You from every evil, immediate and later, what I know of it and what I do not know. I ask You for the good Your servant and Prophet asked You for, and seek refuge from the evil from which Your servant and Prophet sought refuge. I ask You for Paradise and whatever brings near to it in word or deed; I seek refuge in You from the Fire and whatever brings near to it in word or deed; and I ask You to make every decree You decree for me good.
sources: Sunan Ibn Majah 3846; Musnad Ahmad
Sunan Ibn Majah 3846 is displayed as Sahih in the cited contemporary grading and records this as a comprehensive supplication taught by the Prophet ﷺ.

prophetic_halal_sufficiency.title: Sufficiency through What Is Halal
prophetic_halal_sufficiency.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ اكْفِنِي بِحَلَالِكَ عَنْ حَرَامِكَ، وَأَغْنِنِي بِفَضْلِكَ عَمَّنْ سِوَاكَ
prophetic_halal_sufficiency.meaningEn: O Allah, suffice me with what You have made lawful instead of what You have forbidden, and enrich me by Your bounty so that I need none besides You.
sources: Jami‘ at-Tirmidhi 3563
At-Tirmidhi records this report; the commonly displayed grading is Hasan.

prophetic_steadfast_heart.title: Steadfastness of the Heart
prophetic_steadfast_heart.arabic: يَا مُقَلِّبَ الْقُلُوبِ ثَبِّتْ قَلْبِي عَلَى دِينِكَ
prophetic_steadfast_heart.meaningEn: O Changer of the hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion.
sources: Jami‘ at-Tirmidhi 2140
At-Tirmidhi records that the Prophet ﷺ frequently said this supplication and describes the report as Hasan.

prophetic_evil_character.title: Protection from Evil Character and Desires
prophetic_evil_character.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ مُنْكَرَاتِ الْأَخْلَاقِ وَالْأَعْمَالِ وَالْأَهْوَاءِ
prophetic_evil_character.meaningEn: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from evil character, evil deeds, and evil desires.
sources: Jami‘ at-Tirmidhi 3591
At-Tirmidhi described the report as Hasan Gharib; the current Darussalam display on Sunnah.com grades it Sahih.

prophetic_light.title: When Going Out for the Prayer — A Supplication for Light
prophetic_light.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ اجْعَلْ فِي قَلْبِي نُورًا، وَفِي لِسَانِي نُورًا، وَاجْعَلْ فِي سَمْعِي نُورًا، وَاجْعَلْ فِي بَصَرِي نُورًا، وَاجْعَلْ مِنْ خَلْفِي نُورًا، وَمِنْ أَمَامِي نُورًا، وَاجْعَلْ مِنْ فَوْقِي نُورًا، وَمِنْ تَحْتِي نُورًا، اللَّهُمَّ أَعْطِنِي نُورًا
prophetic_light.meaningEn: O Allah, place light in my heart and light in my tongue; place light in my hearing and light in my sight; place light behind me and in front of me; place light above me and below me. O Allah, grant me light.
prophetic_light.transliteration: Allāhummajʿal fī qalbī nūran, wa fī lisānī nūran, wajʿal fī samʿī nūran, wajʿal fī baṣarī nūran, wajʿal min khalfī nūran, wa min amāmī nūran, wajʿal min fawqī nūran, wa min taḥtī nūran. Allāhumma aʿṭinī nūran.
prophetic_light.purposeEn: Asking Allah for light while going out for the prayer.
prophetic_light.whenToSayEn: When going out for the prayer. Sahih Muslim 763l explicitly reports this wording as the Prophet ﷺ went out after the Adhan.
sources: Sahih Muslim 763l

Sahih Muslim explicitly reports this wording as the Prophet ﷺ went out for the prayer after the Muʾadhdhin called. Other authentic light-supplication variants exist; this card deliberately follows one exact recension rather than combining variants into a composite text.

prophetic_forgiveness_abu_bakr.title: Forgiveness and Mercy
prophetic_forgiveness_abu_bakr.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي ظَلَمْتُ نَفْسِي ظُلْمًا كَثِيرًا، وَلَا يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ، فَاغْفِرْ لِي مَغْفِرَةً مِنْ عِنْدِكَ، وَارْحَمْنِي إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْغَفُورُ الرَّحِيمُ
prophetic_forgiveness_abu_bakr.meaningEn: O Allah, I have greatly wronged myself, and none forgives sins except You. Grant me forgiveness from You and have mercy on me; You are the Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.
prophetic_forgiveness_abu_bakr.transliteration: Allāhumma innī ẓalamtu nafsī ẓulman kathīran, wa lā yaghfirudh-dhunūba illā anta, faghfir lī maghfiratan min ʿindika, warḥamnī, innaka antal-Ghafūrur-Raḥīm.
prophetic_forgiveness_abu_bakr.whenToSayEn: Within the prayer. The cited hadith teaches it for salah but does not itself specify one exact position.
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 834; Sahih Muslim 2705
The Prophet ﷺ taught this supplication to Abu Bakr for use in prayer; it is recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim.

prophetic_four_trials.title: Protection from Four Great Trials
prophetic_four_trials.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ عَذَابِ الْقَبْرِ، وَمِنْ عَذَابِ النَّارِ، وَمِنْ فِتْنَةِ الْمَحْيَا وَالْمَمَاتِ، وَمِنْ فِتْنَةِ الْمَسِيحِ الدَّجَّالِ
prophetic_four_trials.meaningEn: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the punishment of the grave, from the punishment of the Fire, from the trials of life and death, and from the trial of the False Messiah, the Dajjal.
prophetic_four_trials.transliteration: Allāhumma innī aʿūdhu bika min ʿadhābil-qabr, wa min ʿadhābin-nār, wa min fitnatil-maḥyā wal-mamāt, wa min fitnatil-Masīḥid-Dajjāl.
prophetic_four_trials.whenToSayEn: After the tashahhud, before ending the prayer with salam.
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 1377; Sahih Muslim 588

Recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim. Sahih Muslim also preserves an authentic wording using “the evil of the trial of the Dajjal.” The report is connected to seeking refuge after the tashahhud in prayer.

daily_garment_wear.title: When Wearing a Garment
daily_garment_wear.arabic: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي كَسَانِي هَذَا الثَّوْبَ وَرَزَقَنِيهِ مِنْ غَيْرِ حَوْلٍ مِنِّي وَلَا قُوَّةٍ
daily_garment_wear.meaningEn: All praise is for Allah Who clothed me with this garment and provided it for me without any might or power on my part.
daily_garment_wear.transliteration: Al-ḥamdu lillāhilladhī kasānī hādhath-thawba wa razaqanīhi min ghayri ḥawlin minnī wa lā quwwah.
daily_garment_wear.purposeEn: Praising Allah for the provision of clothing.
sources: Sunan Abi Dawud 4023
Al-Albani graded the report Hasan while excluding the transmitted addition about later sins. The app stores the supplication itself and does not attach the rejected extension.

daily_new_garment.title: When Wearing a New Garment
daily_new_garment.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ لَكَ الْحَمْدُ أَنْتَ كَسَوْتَنِيهِ، أَسْأَلُكَ مِنْ خَيْرِهِ وَخَيْرِ مَا صُنِعَ لَهُ، وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّهِ وَشَرِّ مَا صُنِعَ لَهُ
daily_new_garment.meaningEn: O Allah, to You belongs all praise. You clothed me with it. I ask You for its good and the good for which it was made, and I seek refuge in You from its evil and the evil for which it was made.
daily_new_garment.transliteration: Allāhumma lakal-ḥamdu anta kasawtanīhi, asʾaluka min khayrihi wa khayri mā ṣuniʿa lahu, wa aʿūdhu bika min sharrihi wa sharri mā ṣuniʿa lahu.
daily_new_garment.purposeEn: Praising Allah and asking for the good of a new garment while seeking refuge from its evil.
daily_new_garment.whenToSayEn: When putting on a new garment.
sources: Sunan Abi Dawud 4020
The report is graded Sahih by Al-Albani and records this wording when the Prophet ﷺ put on a new garment.

daily_new_garment_companion_congratulati.title: To Someone Wearing a New Garment — Companion Practice
daily_new_garment_companion_congratulati.meaningEn: May you wear it until it wears out, and may Allah Most High replace it.
daily_new_garment_companion_congratulati.purposeEn: A congratulatory phrase reported as the practice of the Companions.
daily_new_garment_companion_congratulati.whenToSayEn: When congratulating someone who has put on a new garment.
sources: Sunan Abi Dawud 4020

Abu Nadrah reports this as what the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ used to say when someone wore a new garment. It is intentionally labeled Companion practice and is not attributed directly to the Prophet ﷺ.

daily_undressing_bismillah.title: Before Undressing — Bismillah
sources: Al-Tabarani, al-Muʿjam al-Awsat; Ibn as-Sunni 274; Sahih al-Jamiʿ 3610

Individual Anas routes contain weakness; Ibn ʿAdi specifically notes Zayd al-ʿAmmi as weak. Al-Albani graded the report Sahih in Sahih al-Jamiʿ 3610 based on the transmitted routes. The app preserves that grading history rather than describing every individual chain as strong.

daily_sleep_name_die_live.title: Before Sleep — In Your Name I Die and Live
daily_sleep_name_die_live.meaningEn: O Allah, in Your name I die and I live.
daily_sleep_name_die_live.purposeEn: A remembrance taught for going to sleep.
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 6314, 6324
Sahih al-Bukhari records this wording for going to bed. The uploaded Daily Essential Duas PDF cites older volume/page numbering; the app stores the traceable hadith numbers instead.

daily_sleep_submit_to_allah.title: Before Sleep — Submit and Entrust Your Affair to Allah
daily_sleep_submit_to_allah.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ أَسْلَمْتُ وَجْهِي إِلَيْكَ، وَفَوَّضْتُ أَمْرِي إِلَيْكَ، وَأَلْجَأْتُ ظَهْرِي إِلَيْكَ، رَغْبَةً وَرَهْبَةً إِلَيْكَ، لَا مَلْجَأَ وَلَا مَنْجَا مِنْكَ إِلَّا إِلَيْكَ، آمَنْتُ بِكِتَابِكَ الَّذِي أَنْزَلْتَ، وَبِنَبِيِّكَ الَّذِي أَرْسَلْتَ
daily_sleep_submit_to_allah.meaningEn: O Allah, I submit myself to You, entrust my affair to You, and place my back in reliance upon You, in hope and fear of You. There is no refuge or escape from You except to You. I believe in Your Book which You revealed and Your Prophet whom You sent.
daily_sleep_submit_to_allah.transliteration: Allāhumma aslamtu wajhī ilayk, wa fawwaḍtu amrī ilayk, wa aljaʾtu ẓahrī ilayk, raghbatan wa rahbatan ilayk. Lā maljaʾa wa lā manjā minka illā ilayk. Āmantu bikitābikal-ladhī anzalta, wa binabiyyikal-ladhī arsalta.
daily_sleep_submit_to_allah.purposeEn: A bedtime supplication of submission, reliance, hope, fear, and faith.
daily_sleep_submit_to_allah.whenToSayEn: At bedtime after performing wudu and lying on the right side; the cited hadith says to make these the last words spoken before sleep.
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 6311
The hadith is in Sahih al-Bukhari. The Prophet ﷺ specifically corrected the memorized wording from 'Your Messenger' to 'Your Prophet'; the app preserves 'Your Prophet' exactly.

daily_night_turning_tawhid.title: When Turning Restlessly During the Night — Grading Differs
daily_night_turning_tawhid.arabic: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ الْوَاحِدُ الْقَهَّارُ، رَبُّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا، الْعَزِيزُ الْغَفَّارُ
daily_night_turning_tawhid.meaningEn: None has the right to be worshipped except Allah, the One, the All-Subduer; Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, the Almighty, the Ever-Forgiving.
daily_night_turning_tawhid.transliteration: Lā ilāha illallāhul-Wāḥidul-Qahhār, Rabbus-samāwāti wal-arḍi wa mā baynahumā, al-ʿAzīzul-Ghaffār.
daily_night_turning_tawhid.purposeEn: A reported night remembrance, kept with the hadith-grading disagreement visible.
daily_night_turning_tawhid.whenToSayEn: When turning/restlessly moving during the night.
sources: An-Nasaʾi, as-Sunan al-Kubra 10700; Sahih Ibn Hibban 5530; Sahih al-Jamiʿ 4693

Reported from ʿAʾishah. Al-Albani graded it Sahih in Sahih al-Jamiʿ 4693. Al-Wadiʿi, citing Abu Hatim and Abu Zurʿah, recorded a criticism that the connected attribution is mistaken and that it is from ʿUrwah's statement. The app therefore preserves the grading disagreement rather than presenting the report as unanimously authenticated.

daily_sleep_fright_perfect_words.title: When Frightened During Sleep — Refuge in Allah's Perfect Words
daily_sleep_fright_perfect_words.arabic: أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّاتِ مِنْ غَضَبِهِ وَعِقَابِهِ وَشَرِّ عِبَادِهِ، وَمِنْ هَمَزَاتِ الشَّيَاطِينِ وَأَنْ يَحْضُرُونِ
daily_sleep_fright_perfect_words.meaningEn: I seek refuge in Allah's perfect words from His anger and His punishment, from the evil of His servants, from the incitements of the devils, and from their presence.
daily_sleep_fright_perfect_words.transliteration: Aʿūdhu bikalimātillāhit-tāmmāti min ghaḍabihī wa ʿiqābihī wa sharri ʿibādihī, wa min hamazātish-shayāṭīni wa an yaḥḍurūn.
daily_sleep_fright_perfect_words.purposeEn: Seeking Allah's protection when frightened during sleep.
daily_sleep_fright_perfect_words.whenToSayEn: When experiencing fright or alarm during sleep.
sources: Jamiʿ at-Tirmidhi 3528; Sahih at-Targhib 1601; Sunan Abi Dawud 3893

At-Tirmidhi called his route Hasan Gharib while the current Darussalam display grades it Daʿif. Al-Albani graded the sleep-fright wording Hasan li-ghayrihi in Sahih at-Targhib 1601 / Hasan in Sahih al-Jamiʿ 701. Abu Dawud 3893 has a closely related wording and Al-Albani grades its supplication Hasan while excluding the later Companion practice. The app preserves this grading difference rather than labeling the Tirmidhi route unconditionally Sahih. Wording differs between copies: Sahih at-Targhib 1601, which states the wording is at-Tirmidhi's, reads at-tāmmāt as shown here, while the Sunnah.com text of at-Tirmidhi 3528 and Abu Dawud 3893 read at-tāmmah.

daily_waking_praise_return.title: Upon Waking — Praise and Resurrection
daily_waking_praise_return.arabic: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَحْيَانَا بَعْدَ مَا أَمَاتَنَا وَإِلَيْهِ النُّشُورُ
daily_waking_praise_return.meaningEn: All praise is for Allah Who gave us life after causing us to die, and to Him is the resurrection.
daily_waking_praise_return.transliteration: Al-ḥamdu lillāhilladhī aḥyānā baʿda mā amātanā wa ilayhin-nushūr.
daily_waking_praise_return.purposeEn: Praising Allah upon waking and remembering the resurrection.
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 6314, 6324
Recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari as the remembrance said upon waking.

daily_bathroom_enter.title: Before Entering the Bathroom
daily_bathroom_enter.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ الْخُبُثِ وَالْخَبَائِثِ
daily_bathroom_enter.meaningEn: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from evil and the evil ones.
daily_bathroom_enter.transliteration: Allāhumma innī aʿūdhu bika minal-khubthi wal-khabāʾith.
daily_bathroom_enter.purposeEn: Seeking Allah's protection before entering the bathroom.
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 142

This card follows the core wording recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari 142. Some collections append Bismillah from a separate report; it is not merged into this Sahih-Bukhari card so the source wording and grading remain distinct.

daily_bathroom_exit.title: After Leaving the Bathroom — Seeking Forgiveness
daily_bathroom_exit.purposeEn: Seeking Allah's forgiveness after leaving the bathroom.
sources: Jamiʿ at-Tirmidhi 7; Hisn al-Muslim 11

At-Tirmidhi records Ghufranaka; he described the report as Hasan Gharib and the current Darussalam display grades it Sahih. The uploaded PDF appends an additional praise sentence; that extra sentence is not imported as part of this entry.

daily_wudu_start.title: Before Wudu
sources: Sunan Abi Dawud 101; Hisn al-Muslim 12

Abu Dawud 101 is graded Sahih by Al-Albani and establishes mentioning Allah's Name at the beginning of wudu. Hisn al-Muslim 12 gives the practical wording Bismillah; the app does not expand it into the full Basmala without a matching citation.

daily_wudu_complete.title: After Wudu — Testimony of Faith
daily_wudu_complete.arabic: أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، وَأَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا عَبْدُهُ وَرَسُولُهُ
daily_wudu_complete.meaningEn: I bear witness that none has the right to be worshipped except Allah alone, with no partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger.
daily_wudu_complete.transliteration: Ash-hadu an lā ilāha illallāhu waḥdahu lā sharīka lah, wa ash-hadu anna Muḥammadan ʿabduhu wa rasūluh.
daily_wudu_complete.purposeEn: A testimony of faith said after completing wudu.
sources: Sahih Muslim 234b; Hisn al-Muslim 13
The testimony is recorded in Sahih Muslim and preserved in Hisn al-Muslim 13.

daily_masjid_enter.title: Upon Entering the Masjid
daily_masjid_enter.arabic: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ، وَالصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ عَلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ، اللَّهُمَّ افْتَحْ لِي أَبْوَابَ رَحْمَتِكَ
daily_masjid_enter.meaningEn: In the name of Allah, and blessings and peace be upon the Messenger of Allah. O Allah, open for me the gates of Your mercy.
daily_masjid_enter.transliteration: Bismillāh, waṣ-ṣalātu was-salāmu ʿalā Rasūlillāh. Allāhummaftaḥ lī abwāba raḥmatik.
daily_masjid_enter.purposeEn: Sending peace and blessings upon the Prophet ﷺ and asking Allah for His mercy when entering the masjid.
sources: Hisn al-Muslim 20; Sahih Muslim 713a; Sunan Ibn Majah 772
The core request to open the gates of mercy is established in Sahih Muslim, and Ibn Majah 772 records sending peace upon the Prophet ﷺ before it. Hisn al-Muslim preserves the combined remembrance.

daily_masjid_exit.title: Upon Leaving the Masjid
daily_masjid_exit.arabic: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ، وَالصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ عَلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ، اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ مِنْ فَضْلِكَ
daily_masjid_exit.meaningEn: In the name of Allah, and blessings and peace be upon the Messenger of Allah. O Allah, I ask You from Your bounty.
daily_masjid_exit.transliteration: Bismillāh, waṣ-ṣalātu was-salāmu ʿalā Rasūlillāh. Allāhumma innī asʾaluka min faḍlik.
daily_masjid_exit.purposeEn: Asking Allah for His bounty when leaving the masjid.
sources: Hisn al-Muslim 21; Sahih Muslim 713a; Sunan Ibn Majah 772
The request for Allah's bounty is established in the cited mosque narrations. Hisn al-Muslim 21 preserves the combined remembrance used here.

daily_food_before.title: Before Eating
daily_food_before.whenToSayEn: At the beginning of a meal.
sources: Sunan Abi Dawud 3767; Hisn al-Muslim 178
Abu Dawud 3767 is graded Sahih by Al-Albani and instructs mentioning Allah's name when beginning to eat.

daily_food_forgot_bismillah.title: If Bismillah Was Forgotten at the Start of Eating
daily_food_forgot_bismillah.meaningEn: In the name of Allah at its beginning and its end.
daily_food_forgot_bismillah.purposeEn: The remembrance taught for someone who forgot to mention Allah's name at the start of eating.
daily_food_forgot_bismillah.whenToSayEn: When remembering during a meal that Bismillah was omitted at the beginning.
sources: Sunan Abi Dawud 3767; Hisn al-Muslim 178
Abu Dawud 3767 is graded Sahih by Al-Albani and gives this wording for remembering after the meal has begun.

daily_food_after_provision.title: After Eating — Praise for Provision
daily_food_after_provision.arabic: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَطْعَمَنِي هَذَا وَرَزَقَنِيهِ مِنْ غَيْرِ حَوْلٍ مِنِّي وَلَا قُوَّةٍ
daily_food_after_provision.meaningEn: All praise is for Allah Who fed me this and provided it for me without any might or power from me.
daily_food_after_provision.purposeEn: Praising Allah for providing the meal.
sources: Jamiʿ at-Tirmidhi 3458
At-Tirmidhi called the report Hasan Gharib; the current Darussalam display grades it Hasan.

daily_food_after_fed_drink_muslim.title: After Eating — Reported Praise (Weak Chain)
daily_food_after_fed_drink_muslim.arabic: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَطْعَمَنَا وَسَقَانَا وَجَعَلَنَا مُسْلِمِينَ
daily_food_after_fed_drink_muslim.meaningEn: All praise is for Allah Who fed us, gave us drink, and made us Muslims.
daily_food_after_fed_drink_muslim.purposeEn: Included because it appears in the uploaded PDF, with its weak grading made explicit rather than presented as an established authenticated practice.
daily_food_after_fed_drink_muslim.whenToSayEn: Reported after finishing food; the cited route is weak.
sources: Sunan Abi Dawud 3850
The current Sunnah.com/Al-Albani grading for this route is Daʿif. The app therefore labels this entry as a weak report.

daily_food_blessing_when_given.title: When Food Is Given — Blessing for the Food (Grading Differs)
daily_food_blessing_when_given.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ بَارِكْ لَنَا فِيهِ وَأَطْعِمْنَا خَيْرًا مِنْهُ
daily_food_blessing_when_given.meaningEn: O Allah, bless it for us and feed us something better than it.
daily_food_blessing_when_given.purposeEn: A reported supplication when food is provided. The uploaded PDF placed it under after-meal duas; the cited hadith places it when food is given.
daily_food_blessing_when_given.whenToSayEn: When Allah provides food, before eating it.
sources: Jamiʿ at-Tirmidhi 3455

At-Tirmidhi called the report Hasan, while the current Darussalam display on Sunnah.com grades it Daʿif. Al-Albani also graded it Hasan (Sahih at-Tirmidhi 3455; Sunan Abi Dawud 3730), as did Ibn al-Qayyim in Zad al-Maʿad, while Zubair ʿAli Zai judged the chain weak because of ʿAli ibn Zayd. That grading difference is preserved explicitly.

daily_home_leave.title: When Leaving Home
daily_home_leave.arabic: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ، تَوَكَّلْتُ عَلَى اللَّهِ، لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ
daily_home_leave.meaningEn: In the name of Allah; I place my trust in Allah. There is no might and no power except with Allah.
daily_home_leave.transliteration: Bismillāh, tawakkaltu ʿalallāh, lā ḥawla wa lā quwwata illā billāh.
daily_home_leave.purposeEn: Entrusting oneself to Allah when leaving home.
sources: Sunan Abi Dawud 5095; Hisn al-Muslim 16
Abu Dawud 5095 is graded Sahih by Al-Albani and records this wording and the reported protection that follows it.

daily_home_leave_refuge.title: When Leaving Home — Refuge from Error, Slipping, Wrongdoing, and Ignorance
daily_home_leave_refuge.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ أَنْ أَضِلَّ أَوْ أُضَلَّ، أَوْ أَزِلَّ أَوْ أُزَلَّ، أَوْ أَظْلِمَ أَوْ أُظْلَمَ، أَوْ أَجْهَلَ أَوْ يُجْهَلَ عَلَيَّ
daily_home_leave_refuge.meaningEn: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from going astray or being led astray, slipping or being made to slip, wronging or being wronged, acting ignorantly or being treated ignorantly.
daily_home_leave_refuge.transliteration: Allāhumma innī aʿūdhu bika an aḍilla aw uḍalla, aw azilla aw uzalla, aw aẓlima aw uẓlama, aw ajhala aw yujhala ʿalayya.
daily_home_leave_refuge.purposeEn: Seeking Allah's protection from error and wrongdoing when leaving home.
sources: Sunan Abi Dawud 5094
The report is graded Sahih by Al-Albani and records this supplication when the Prophet ﷺ left the house.

daily_home_enter_reported.title: When Entering Home — Reported Formula (Weak Chain)
daily_home_enter_reported.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ خَيْرَ الْمَوْلِجِ وَخَيْرَ الْمَخْرَجِ، بِسْمِ اللَّهِ وَلَجْنَا، وَبِسْمِ اللَّهِ خَرَجْنَا، وَعَلَى اللَّهِ رَبِّنَا تَوَكَّلْنَا
daily_home_enter_reported.meaningEn: O Allah, I ask You for the good of entering and the good of leaving. In the name of Allah we enter, in the name of Allah we leave, and upon Allah our Lord we rely.
daily_home_enter_reported.transliteration: Allāhumma innī as'aluka khayral-mawliji wa khayral-makhraj. Bismillāhi walajnā, wa bismillāhi kharajnā, wa ʿalā Allāhi Rabbinā tawakkalnā.
daily_home_enter_reported.purposeEn: Included from the uploaded PDF with the grading limitation visible. Independently, Sahih Muslim records the general practice of mentioning Allah's name when entering the home.
daily_home_enter_reported.whenToSayEn: Reported for entering one's home; the full cited formula has a weak chain.
sources: Sunan Abi Dawud 5096; Hisn al-Muslim 18

The current Sunnah.com/Al-Albani grading for Abu Dawud 5096 is Daʿif; al-Albani first graded it Sahih and later Daʿif because the chain is interrupted, and Abu Hatim judged it mursal. Ibn Baz said its chain is acceptable (lā baʾsa bihi) and graded it Hasan, as did Ibn Muflih. The Arabic shown is Abu Dawud's full wording, which opens with Allāhumma innī as'aluka khayral-mawlij; Hisn al-Muslim 18 preserves a shorter excerpt without that opening. Sunnah.com vowels al-mawlij with kasra, and some editions read al-mawlaj. Sahih Muslim 2018 independently supports mentioning Allah's name when entering the home and eating.

daily_home_enter_name_of_allah.title: When Entering Home — Mention Allah's Name
daily_home_enter_name_of_allah.purposeEn: A simple tasmiyah representing the Sahih instruction to mention Allah's Name when entering the home; it is not presented as a verbatim longer formula from Muslim 2018a.
daily_home_enter_name_of_allah.practiceEn: Mention Allah's Name when entering. Sahih Muslim 2018a establishes the practice but does not transmit one fixed longer entering-home formula.
sources: Sahih Muslim 2018a

Sahih Muslim states that a person should mention Allah's Name when entering the home and when eating. It does not give a specific longer formula in this report. An-Nawawi wrote in al-Adhkar that it is recommended to say Bismillah when entering one's house and to remember Allah often, and Ibn Baz and ʿAbd al-Muhsin al-ʿAbbad likewise explain this mention of Allah as saying Bismillah. The app therefore keeps this tasmiyah distinct from the weak Abu Dawud 5096 formula already retained with its weakness visible.

daily_travel_return.title: Returning from a Journey — Repentant and Praising
daily_travel_return.meaningEn: We return, repenting, worshipping, and praising our Lord.
daily_travel_return.purposeEn: Remembrance said while returning from a journey.
sources: Sahih Muslim 1345a; Hisn al-Muslim 207, 217
Sahih Muslim records this return-from-travel wording. Hisn al-Muslim also preserves fuller travel and return formulas; this entry retains the phrase specifically shown in the uploaded PDF.

daily_sneeze_praise.title: When You Sneeze
daily_sneeze_praise.purposeEn: The remembrance taught to the person who sneezes.
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 6224
Sahih al-Bukhari records this phrase and the complete three-part sneezing exchange.

daily_sneeze_response.title: Reply to Someone Who Sneezes and Praises Allah
daily_sneeze_response.meaningEn: May Allah have mercy on you.
daily_sneeze_response.purposeEn: The response taught to the listener after the sneezer praises Allah.
daily_sneeze_response.whenToSayEn: After hearing a Muslim sneeze and say Alhamdulillah.
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 6224
Recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari as the second part of the sneezing exchange.

daily_sneezer_reply.title: Sneezer's Reply
daily_sneezer_reply.meaningEn: May Allah guide you and set your affairs right.
daily_sneezer_reply.purposeEn: The reply taught to the sneezer after being prayed for with mercy.
daily_sneezer_reply.whenToSayEn: After someone says Yarhamukallah to the sneezer.
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 6224
Recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari as the final part of the sneezing exchange.

daily_market_remembrance.title: Entering the Market — Reported Remembrance (Grading Differs)
daily_market_remembrance.arabic: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ، يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ، وَهُوَ حَيٌّ لَا يَمُوتُ، بِيَدِهِ الْخَيْرُ، وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
daily_market_remembrance.meaningEn: None has the right to be worshipped except Allah alone, with no partner. His is the dominion and His is the praise. He gives life and causes death; He is Living and does not die. In His hand is all good, and He has power over all things.
daily_market_remembrance.purposeEn: Included because it appears in the uploaded PDF, while keeping the grading disagreement visible and not presenting the reported reward as settled fact.
daily_market_remembrance.whenToSayEn: Reported for entering a marketplace; the cited route is not treated as unconditionally authentic.
sources: Jamiʿ at-Tirmidhi 3428

At-Tirmidhi described the report as Gharib; the current Darussalam display on Sunnah.com grades it Daʿif. Other scholars have discussed supporting routes, so the app preserves the disagreement rather than calling it unconditionally authentic.

daily_intimacy_before.title: Before Marital Intimacy
daily_intimacy_before.arabic: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ، اللَّهُمَّ جَنِّبْنَا الشَّيْطَانَ، وَجَنِّبِ الشَّيْطَانَ مَا رَزَقْتَنَا
daily_intimacy_before.meaningEn: In the name of Allah. O Allah, keep Satan away from us, and keep Satan away from what You provide for us.
daily_intimacy_before.purposeEn: Seeking Allah's protection for the spouses and any child He may decree.
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari; Sahih Muslim; Hisn al-Muslim 192
The supplication and its stated context are recorded in the two Sahih collections and preserved in Hisn al-Muslim 192.

daily_adhan_testimony_contentment.title: Upon Hearing the Adhan — Testimony and Contentment
daily_adhan_testimony_contentment.arabic: أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، وَأَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا عَبْدُهُ وَرَسُولُهُ، رَضِيتُ بِاللَّهِ رَبًّا، وَبِمُحَمَّدٍ رَسُولًا، وَبِالْإِسْلَامِ دِينًا
daily_adhan_testimony_contentment.meaningEn: I testify that none has the right to be worshipped except Allah alone with no partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. I am pleased with Allah as Lord, Muhammad as Messenger, and Islam as religion.
daily_adhan_testimony_contentment.transliteration: Ash-hadu an lā ilāha illallāhu waḥdahu lā sharīka lah, wa anna Muḥammadan ʿabduhu wa rasūluh. Raḍītu billāhi Rabban, wa bi-Muḥammadin Rasūlan, wa bil-Islāmi dīnan.
daily_adhan_testimony_contentment.purposeEn: A remembrance taught for the listener upon hearing the Muʾadhdhin.
sources: Sahih Muslim 386
Sahih Muslim records this wording for the person hearing the Muʾadhdhin and reports forgiveness of sins for saying it.

daily_after_adhan.title: After the Adhan — Al-Wasilah for the Prophet ﷺ
daily_after_adhan.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ رَبَّ هَذِهِ الدَّعْوَةِ التَّامَّةِ وَالصَّلَاةِ الْقَائِمَةِ، آتِ مُحَمَّدًا الْوَسِيلَةَ وَالْفَضِيلَةَ، وَابْعَثْهُ مَقَامًا مَحْمُودًا الَّذِي وَعَدْتَهُ
daily_after_adhan.meaningEn: O Allah, Lord of this perfect call and the prayer to be established, grant Muhammad the Wasilah and excellence, and raise him to the praised station You promised him.
daily_after_adhan.transliteration: Allāhumma Rabba hādhihid-daʿwatit-tāmmati waṣ-ṣalātil-qāʾimah, āti Muḥammadanil-wasīlata wal-faḍīlah, wabʿath-hu maqāman maḥmūdan alladhī waʿadtah.
daily_after_adhan.purposeEn: Asking Allah to grant the Prophet ﷺ al-Wasilah and the praised station after the Adhan.
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 614
This entry follows the wording of Sahih al-Bukhari 614. The uploaded PDF includes the addition 'You do not break the promise'; that addition is not part of the Bukhari 614 wording used here.

daily_janazah_living_dead.title: Janazah — Forgive Our Living and Our Dead
daily_janazah_living_dead.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لِحَيِّنَا وَمَيِّتِنَا، وَشَاهِدِنَا وَغَائِبِنَا، وَصَغِيرِنَا وَكَبِيرِنَا، وَذَكَرِنَا وَأُنْثَانَا، اللَّهُمَّ مَنْ أَحْيَيْتَهُ مِنَّا فَأَحْيِهِ عَلَى الْإِسْلَامِ، وَمَنْ تَوَفَّيْتَهُ مِنَّا فَتَوَفَّهُ عَلَى الْإِيمَانِ، اللَّهُمَّ لَا تَحْرِمْنَا أَجْرَهُ وَلَا تُضِلَّنَا بَعْدَهُ
daily_janazah_living_dead.meaningEn: O Allah, forgive our living and our dead, those present and absent, our young and old, our males and females. O Allah, whoever You keep alive among us, keep them alive upon Islam; whoever You cause to die among us, cause them to die upon faith. O Allah, do not deprive us of the deceased's reward and do not let us go astray after them.
daily_janazah_living_dead.purposeEn: A comprehensive supplication for the deceased and the Muslim community in the Janazah prayer.
sources: Sunan Ibn Majah 1498
The current Darussalam display grades this route Hasan. Closely related variants are also transmitted in other collections.

daily_two_beloved_phrases.title: Two Phrases Beloved to the Most Merciful
daily_two_beloved_phrases.arabic: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ الْعَظِيمِ، سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ
daily_two_beloved_phrases.meaningEn: Glory be to Allah, the Magnificent. Glory and praise be to Allah.
daily_two_beloved_phrases.purposeEn: Two phrases described as light on the tongue, heavy in the balance, and beloved to the Most Merciful.
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 6406
Recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari with the stated virtue.

daily_laylat_al_qadr_pardon.title: Laylat al-Qadr — Asking Allah for Pardon
daily_laylat_al_qadr_pardon.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنَّكَ عَفُوٌّ تُحِبُّ الْعَفْوَ فَاعْفُ عَنِّي
daily_laylat_al_qadr_pardon.meaningEn: O Allah, You are Pardoning and You love pardon, so pardon me.
daily_laylat_al_qadr_pardon.purposeEn: The supplication taught to Aishah for Laylat al-Qadr.
daily_laylat_al_qadr_pardon.whenToSayEn: On Laylat al-Qadr and as a general supplication for pardon.
sources: Jamiʿ at-Tirmidhi 3513

At-Tirmidhi called the report Hasan Sahih and the current Darussalam display grades it Sahih. Some printed transmissions include the word Karim; the uploaded PDF and common core wording used here omit that bracketed addition.

daily_no_might_power.title: There Is No Might nor Power Except with Allah
daily_no_might_power.arabic: لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ
daily_no_might_power.meaningEn: There is no might and no power except with Allah.
daily_no_might_power.transliteration: Lā ḥawla wa lā quwwata illā billāh.
daily_no_might_power.purposeEn: A general dhikr described as a treasure from Paradise and the authentic response to the two Ḥayya phrases of the Adhan.
daily_no_might_power.whenToSayEn: General remembrance at any time; during the Adhan, say it in response to Ḥayya ʿalaṣ-ṣalāh and Ḥayya ʿalal-falāḥ.
daily_no_might_power.practiceEn: During the Adhan, repeat the Muʾadhdhin's words except respond to the two Ḥayya calls with this phrase, as detailed in Sahih Muslim 385.
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 6384, 6409, 6610
Sahih al-Bukhari records this remembrance and describes it as a treasure from the treasures of Paradise.
Sahih Muslim 385
Sahih Muslim gives this exact response when the Muʾadhdhin says Ḥayya ʿalaṣ-ṣalāh and Ḥayya ʿalal-falāḥ.

daily_four_beloved_words.title: Four Words Beloved to Allah
daily_four_beloved_words.arabic: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، وَلَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ، وَاللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ
daily_four_beloved_words.meaningEn: Glory be to Allah; all praise is for Allah; none has the right to be worshipped except Allah; Allah is the Greatest.
daily_four_beloved_words.purposeEn: Four phrases described as among the words dearest to Allah.
sources: Sahih Muslim 2137a
Sahih Muslim explicitly names these four phrases and says there is no harm in whichever one is begun with.

daily_protection_hellfire_after_fajr_mag.title: After Fajr/Maghrib — Reported Protection from Hellfire (Weak Route)
daily_protection_hellfire_after_fajr_mag.meaningEn: O Allah, protect me from the Fire.
daily_protection_hellfire_after_fajr_mag.purposeEn: A sound supplication in meaning; the specific seven-times-after-Fajr/Maghrib virtue in the cited route is weak.
daily_protection_hellfire_after_fajr_mag.whenToSayEn: The cited weak report places it after Fajr and Maghrib.
daily_protection_hellfire_after_fajr_mag.practiceEn: The cited weak report says seven times. It is shown for source transparency, not presented as a settled authenticated practice.
sources: Sunan Abi Dawud 5079
The current Sunnah.com/Al-Albani grading for this report is Daʿif. The app does not present the specific timing, repetition count, or promised virtue as established Sahih practice.

daily_refuge_from_shirk.title: Protection from Knowingly or Unknowingly Associating Partners
daily_refuge_from_shirk.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ أَنْ أُشْرِكَ بِكَ وَأَنَا أَعْلَمُ، وَأَسْتَغْفِرُكَ لِمَا لَا أَعْلَمُ
daily_refuge_from_shirk.meaningEn: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from associating anything with You knowingly, and I seek Your forgiveness for what I do not know.
daily_refuge_from_shirk.purposeEn: Seeking protection from deliberate shirk and forgiveness for what is unknown to oneself.
daily_refuge_from_shirk.whenToSayEn: General supplication for protection from shirk.
sources: Musnad Ahmad 4/403; Hisn al-Muslim 203
Hisn al-Muslim cites Al-Albani's authentication through Sahih al-Jami and Sahih at-Targhib wat-Tarhib.

daily_children_protection.title: Protection for Children
daily_children_protection.arabic: أُعِيذُكُمَا بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّةِ مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْطَانٍ وَهَامَّةٍ، وَمِنْ كُلِّ عَيْنٍ لَامَّةٍ
daily_children_protection.meaningEn: I seek refuge for you both in Allah's perfect words from every devil and harmful creature, and from every harmful envious eye.
daily_children_protection.purposeEn: The protection the Prophet ﷺ used for al-Hasan and al-Husayn.
daily_children_protection.whenToSayEn: When seeking Allah's protection for children.
